validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki was 403 to automated fetch (Cloudflare) and wiki_citations.json is empty for this scope, so this row had zero prior refs to re-check (all 9 ref_cols came back MISSING_REF) -- treated as a from-scratch existence check per scope notes. Every generic open-web search on 'Badin Gas Pipeline' returned an AI summary that just recites GEM's own numbers (200 MMSCFD/101 km/18 in/'Indus Left Bank Pipeline System') because gem.wiki dominates the SERP for this exact name -- I did NOT accept any of those summaries at face value and instead chased primary documents directly. FOUND TWO GENUINELY INDEPENDENT PRIMARY SOURCES that name this exact segment with matching specs: (1) SSGC's own live 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization' page (raw HTML table row, verified by curl+grep, not just an AI summary): '18″ dia. x100 Km Badin Pipeline Badin-Hyderabad' with available capacity 200 (MMCFD column) -- SSGC is the pipeline's owner/operator, filing this under regulatory capacity-declaration rules. (2) OGRA's (Pakistan's oil & gas regulator -- a separate government body, not SSGC and not GEM) 'State of the Regulated Petroleum Industry 2019-20' report, natural-gas transmission capacity table, SSGC section: '18'' Dia. Badin Pipeline Badin-Hyderabad' with contracted/available capacity 200/200. This is a genuinely independent second organization (regulator vs. operator) naming the identical segment with identical diameter, identical route, identical capacity. Route (Badin->Hyderabad), diameter (18in), capacity (200 MMcf/d), classification (transmission, listed under both sources' 'Transmission System' tables), fuel (natural gas, OGRA's NATURAL GAS section) and owner (SSGC -- the filer of both documents' underlying network) are all corroborated. Length: SSGC's page rounds to '100 Km' vs GEM's 101.00 km -- a ~1% rounding difference, not a material disagreement, so NOT flagged as a spec concern. Duplicate check against the 63-pipeline roster: no other row plausibly matches this route/spec -- the neighboring SSGC table row '24″dia. x84 Km HQ2-TandoAdam' (85 MMCFD) matches roster row P4017 almost exactly, which is reassuring corroboration of the roster generally but confirms P4018 (Badin-Hyderabad, 200 MMCFD, 18in) is a distinct segment, not a relabeling of P4017 or any other row. Caveat: StartYear1=1988 could not be independently confirmed or contradicted -- no source found gives a construction/commissioning year for this specific segment (WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before I could dig further); leaving it unresolved rather than fabricating support.
